thread:
alex (support): Hey team, escalation from June at Acme Media — their streaming SSE connections are frequently disconnecting mid-response and sometimes reconnects produce duplicated partial tokens. Customer reports: ~3-8% of streams end with a partial chunk, client retries cause duplicate text, and they see billing tokens charged for duplicates. They provided a minimal repro and a packet capture. 

june (customer): repro steps I ran:
1) curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
   https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/chat
2) send a 1k token prompt, wait ~7-20s, about 1/25 attempts the stream stops with no final event and client reconnects. When reconnecting the client gets the tail tokens again.

alex (support): Attached pcap and request_id in support ticket: req_0a1b2c3d. pcap link: https://internal-artifacts/acme/1769456789.pcap (uploaded by devops-bot). Also saw the customer mention increased 95th perc latency before disconnects.

devops-bot: Uploaded pcap: https://internal-artifacts/acme/1769456789.pcap; trace id: trace-09a7f; service spans: runtime.proxy -> runtime.handler -> network-egress.

maria (eng-runtime): Thanks, looking. Quick questions: is this only SSE (text/event-stream) or also websocket/streaming? Any request headers like `Connection: keep-alive` or proxies in front?

june (customer): only SSE right now, they go through a GCP LB then Cloudflare in front. We set `Connection: keep-alive`, and `timeout: 70s` on their LB.

sam (eng-sre): pinging infra metrics: I pulled `streaming.sse.disconnect_rate{route="/v1/streams/chat"}` for Acme's org → spike from 0.8% baseline to 4.5% in that window. Also `egress.write_errors` shows occasional EPIPE in the runtime. 

maria (eng-runtime): EPIPE + duplicate tokens suggests the client-side reconnect is replaying from last acked token but our runtime didn't persist a final commit for the session (KV cache flush). Could be a race where write fails during final chunk, handler exits before marking session finished. Need logs for req_0a1b2c3d.

alex (support): I uploaded debug logs from customer timeframe (log bundle id: logs-1769456789.tar.gz). Key excerpts: 
```
[2026-03-10T14:12:02Z] req=req_0a1b2c3d handler:start session_id=sess-77
[2026-03-10T14:12:22Z] req=req_0a1b2c3d runtime:stream:write err=broken pipe remote_ip=1.2.3.4
[2026-03-10T14:12:22Z] req=req_0a1b2c3d handler:exit reason=client_disconnect bytes_sent=1432
```

maria (eng-runtime): That log lines up. Hypothesis: large response, runtime attempts to write final token batch, underlying TCP connection closed by upstream (LB/Cloudflare) mid-write; our handler marks bytes_sent but does not atomically mark session complete, leaving the session in an intermediate state. Client reconnects and retries from last token, our session replay gives tail tokens again (duplicates). Billing is counted when tokens are produced, so duplicates get charged.

sam (eng-sre): Two possible contributing factors: 1) LB health or Idle timeout cutting longer SSE connections (their LB timeout is 70s, but Cloudflare may have a lower boundary). 2) Backpressure/backlog causing the runtime to block on writes and trigger kernel-level EPIPE when upstream closes. I can check LB logs for FIN/RST pattern.

alex (support): Customer also attached `tcpdump` snippet showing a FIN sent by Cloudflare within the same second as the broken pipe.

maria (eng-runtime): Action plan:
- Enable request-level debug for this org for 24h to capture full write traces and session state transitions (will add sampling for `req_0a1b2c3d`).
- Add a temporary guard to mark session completed atomically before final write ack (hotfix attempt) — low-risk patch if we can ensure it's idempotent.
- Produce a reproducer inside our staging with a flaky proxy that sends FIN mid-write. I can simulate with `socat` / `netcat` to close socket during streaming.

sam (eng-sre): I'll pull LB logs for Acme's IP ranges. Also will add metric alert for `streaming.sse.write_eip_fail_ratio`. For immediate mitigation, recommend customer set `max_idle` and `keepalive` headers to keep proxy alive (and ensure Cloudflare timeout >= 120s).

june (customer): We can try raising timeouts but want Redwood to fix replay/duplicate billing. Our legal team flagged duplicate charges.

alex (support): For billing: we'll create a billing credit with reference to req_0a1b2c3d and similar cases once engineering confirms duplicates are from server-side non-idempotent behavior. I'll need a list of affected request ids and timestamps.

maria (eng-runtime): Temporary telemetry queries for the window: 
```
# affected sessions where write_error != "" AND session_state != COMPLETED
SELECT req_id, org_id, timestamp FROM runtime.logs WHERE write_error IS NOT NULL AND session_state != 'COMPLETED' AND org_id='acme'
```
I ran that query on the debug logs and found 12 sessions in the past 48h. I'll attach ids to the ticket.

sam (eng-sre): LB logs show Cloudflare sent `FIN, ACK` at 14:12:22 for that TCP stream, immediately followed by our kernel EPIPE. Matches the pcap. Cloudflare's documented idle timeout for streaming connections is 60s on their edge. That would explain partial disconnects for long responses.

maria (eng-runtime): Long-term fix: make finalization path idempotent so clients replaying won't double-bill. Short-term: hotfix to persist session completion before last write return (requires careful ordering). Also add server-side dedupe: we can detect duplicate resumed sessions by comparing final KV cache hash and suppress re-emission if identical (cheap guard).

alex (support): Next steps summarized for ticket:
- Support: create billing credit for affected req ids (pending engineering confirmation).
- Eng-runtime (maria): enable debug sampling, attempt hotfix, simulate flaky proxy in staging.
- Eng-sre (sam): confirm Cloudflare timeout and notify customer about recommended LB/config updates.
- Customer (june): raise edge timeout to 120s and report if disconnect rate drops.

june (customer): Will try config change and report back. Thanks all. :pray:

maria (eng-runtime): I'll push debug sampling today and start a canary hotfix branch. If we can reproduce in staging with a forced FIN, we should be able to validate the idempotent commit. Will report status in this thread by EOD.

alex (support): Thanks — marking as high priority. If folks want the pcap or logs I uploaded earlier, link again: https://internal-artifacts/acme/1769456789.pcap and https://internal-artifacts/acme/logs-1769456789.tar.gz

devops-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-03010 streaming-sse-disconnects-acme (priority: P2).

maria (eng-runtime): Quick note from initial staging repro: forcing FIN at 50-60s reliably reproduces a `handler:exit` before commit. Patch ready for review that flips commit order and adds an idempotent marker. Will request fast-track review.

alex (support): Awesome. I'll keep customer updated. closing loop once hotfix validated and billing credits issued. :white_check_mark:

june (customer): Confirmed - after raising timeout to 120s yesterday, disconnect rate dropped dramatically. We'll keep monitoring and await your fix for duplicate billing.

sam (eng-sre): I'll leave the metric alert muted for 24h while customer changes take effect, then re-evaluate.

maria (eng-runtime): Patch landed to canary and tests passing — will schedule rollout to dedicated runtime canary tomorrow and monitor `streaming.sse.duplicate_emission_rate`.

alex (support): Thanks team. Closing thread when postmortem is available.
